host_device.name: iPhone 4 (GSM)
host_device.notes: The user's device. Currently on iOS 4.1, downgraded untethered with Legacy iOS Kit (likely powdersn0w-based). On-NAND bootloaders must NOT be overwritten or the untethered 4.1 boot breaks.

firmware_targets.purpose: First iOS with iPhone 4 support. Proves the build + tethered-boot pipeline end to end before any hybrid work.
firmware_targets.boot_method: tethered (limera1n / loaded from host over USB)

firmware_targets.purpose: Source of the real iPhone 4 bootchain for the hybrid: LLB, iBoot, iBSS, iBEC, DeviceTree, kernelcache. These know the A4 hardware.
Source of the iOS 3 userland (SpringBoard, apps, frameworks) laid on top of the iPhone 4 bootchain. Closest iOS 3 build to the 4.0 kernel, so best odds of booting.

hard_limits.floor: iOS 4.0 is the lowest version with native iPhone 4 support. Anything below it (3.x) has no bootloaders, kernel or drivers for this hardware and can only ever be attempted as a hybrid.
hard_limits.ceiling: iOS 7.1.2 is the last version Apple released for iPhone 4.
hard_limits.baseband: The baseband (modem) firmware is never flashed or modified. It is not part of any build or boot step here.
hard_limits.on_nand_bootloaders: The experimental OS boots from host RAM over USB. The phone's on-NAND LLB/iBoot are never rewritten, so the untethered 4.1 install stays intact.
